_milan_kvasnicka_: Viktor Kvasnicka arrived with the evening ration party, carrying a letter he never sent and a borrowed greatcoat two sizes too big.
Viktor Kvasnicka was in the first hundred. The old hands in R-F13 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
Viktor Kvasnicka wrote a letter home. He wrote about the weather. He did not write about the rats.
Viktor Kvasnicka counted the ladles in the pot against the men in the queue. The final serving took some careful scraping.

Viktor Kvasnicka began repairing a blanket with scraps from ruined clothing. The first patch is a different colour from everything else. Verdel Ridge is lost. Viktor Kvasnicka heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
Word of Viktor Kvasnicka's blanket spread. A strip of lining and a square from an old scarf arrived without explanation.
coletonmartin: Dorian Coletonmarti reported to S-F15 with a frozen apple sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
The men argued about whether fish sleep. Dorian Coletonmarti said yes, and was made to explain how anyone could tell.
After what happened at Verdel Ridge, Dorian Coletonmarti asked to serve as a sapper. Nobody argued.

The parcel for Dorian Coletonmarti contained six left socks. By supper, he had found three men willing to trade. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Dorian Coletonmarti stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
A man asked Dorian Coletonmarti to describe Wyvern Cross without mentioning the weather. He began with the steepest street and ended with the cheapest lunch.
yoollyfox: Bram Yoollyfox arrived with the evening ration party, carrying a pressed cornflower and a borrowed greatcoat two sizes too big.
The first hundred were recognised, and Bram Yoollyfox was among them. He wrote the news on the back of an unfinished letter.
The sergeant read out the order: Verdel Ridge has fallen, hold the line. Bram Yoollyfox looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
A shell landed square in R-F9. They found Bram Yoollyfox alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. The surgeon worked on Bram Yoollyfox until the lamp ran dry. It was not enough.

The House of Yoollyfox sent another. Dorian Yoollyfox, older brother of Bram Yoollyfox, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence. First Wave. Dorian Yoollyfox signed when the ink on the posters was still fresh. He keeps the ribbon wrapped in oilcloth with a pressed cornflower.
